meta.title: Saint Jude Initial World-State Seed (1975 snapshot)
meta.status: starting snapshot back-dated five years from the 1980 codex; for owner review
meta.authority_rule: The Saint Jude bible outranks this seed. Campaign history may add facts but may not rewrite setting canon.
meta.calendar_rule: Gregorian; day 0 is Wednesday 1 January 1975; birth_day is authoritative arithmetic and birth_date its rendering.
meta.back_dating_rule: Everyone is exactly five years younger than the codex's 1980 age; posts are what the man plausibly held in 1975.
meta.no_pressures_rule: No pressures, secrets, deadlines or plot hooks are stored; motives are ordinary traits.

judgement_calls: Family sizes (80, 70, 50, 65 made men; 300 to 350 associates) are the codex's 1980 estimates reused for 1975 as an assumption.
Giuseppe Vannucci's age (71), Pietro Castellano (74), Pasquale Ferrante (66), Ignazio Pellegrino (60) and other added people are invented to fit the plausible age gap above their successors.
The codex's Corrado 'Junior' Spatafore is renamed Carlo so he is not a second Corrado 'Junior' beside Corrado Bellini.
Darius 'Silk' Holloway is renamed Darius Hollis: 'Holloway' contains 'Hollow', a word the leak scan forbids.
Inky Sal Weiss is renamed Sol Weiss (a Jewish forger would not be Salvatore).
Marty 'the Nose' Breslin, named in the codex, is replaced by Martin Keogh to avoid reusing a real columnist's name.
'Bellacorte State' is Saint Jude State University; the Bellacorte Ready-Mix is Saint Jude Ready-Mix.
The Starlight is an older supper club founded 1957, which fits a 1975 supper club that may later become a disco.
The Vorovskoy Syndicate is small and new (founded 1972) because the Soviet emigre wave began in 1973.

Women are a small minority of the named cast and none holds a formal underworld rank: Lucia Vannucci (matriarch), Teresa Ianelli (ready-mix office manager), Concetta Falcone (numbers banker), Judith Katz (assistant DA), Maureen Tierney (reporter), Margaret Dunleavy (pub owner), Valerie St. Clair (singer).
Nicknames are in public_identity_text as street names; no secret, pressure or plot hook is attached to any of them.
Business valuations in economic_state come from prices_1975.json ranges; they are assumptions, not accounts.

persons.name: Agostino Maranzano
persons.current: Likes the horses at Bayview Downs and the dice, and is usually short of cash.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Augie. Grandfatherly, soft-spoken waterfront counsellor who has advised the family's Dons and organizes the annual St. Jude parish feast.

persons.name: Anthony Russo
persons.current: Discreet, mindful of his clients.
persons.role: Owner of Russo and Sons Funeral Home
persons.public_identity_text: Funeral director known for lavish wakes and for letting people talk in his back rooms.

persons.name: Arkady Volkov
persons.current: Wants his new crew to grow without a war with the Italians.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as the Tailor. Runs Brighton Point fur shops and the Petro-Star fuel depot; polite and patient.

persons.name: Arthur Blum
persons.current: Likes the access the work gives him; careful with money and clients.
persons.role: Attorney; head of Blum and Associates
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Artie the Pen. Sharp, over-worked defence lawyer who serves several families and developers.

persons.name: Arthur Pendergast
persons.current: Wants re-election and a bigger committee.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Artie. State senator whose committee oversees racing and wagering.

persons.name: Aurelio Sciarra
persons.current: Proud of his crews, resents interference from the elders in the way his jobs are run.
persons.role: Capo in the Sabatini Family, construction regime
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Rolly. Gruff capo who runs the family's construction-site crews and the Concrete Club's meetings.

persons.name: Brendan O'Malley
persons.current: Wants blood for his brother, and finds the cautious path hard to stomach.
persons.public_identity_text: Dock worker and Brigades lieutenant whose older brother was killed in the 1973 dock strike massacre.

persons.name: Carlo Spatafore
persons.current: Passed over for capo and resentful of younger earners; prone to beefs and to skimming protected card games out of spite.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Junior. Grizzled, bad-tempered buttonman who hangs out in noisy Mercer Avenue diners and collects high-risk loans.

persons.name: Carmine Sabatini
persons.current: A ruthless institutional pragmatist who prefers taxes and lockouts to killings and wants a quiet, profitable last decade. Reacts hard only when someone threatens the Concrete Club.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Don Carmine, 'the Architect'. Soft-spoken widower who attends 7:00 AM Mass at St. Rocco's, tends his tomato garden in Oakridge and arbitrates construction union disputes over espresso at the Vesuvio.

persons.name: Cesare Ragusa
persons.current: Keeps meticulous ledgers and notes on every family; a cold intelligence officer.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as the Monk. Quiet, ascetic veteran who served eighteen years in Ironhaven alongside Giuseppe Vannucci; lives in a modest rowhouse above a bakery and drinks herbal tea.

persons.name: Concetta Falcone
persons.current: Pays her runners promptly and expects the family to look after her; careful, with a long memory.
persons.role: Associate of the Sabatini Family; runs a Hill numbers bank
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Connie. Widow of a soldier who kept his numbers book after his death; runs a small Hill numbers bank from her kitchen and a candy store.

persons.name: Corrado Bellini
persons.current: Fiercely loyal to Don Carmine; believes the younger generation is the family's source of rot.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Uncle Junior. Semi-retired diplomat who breeds orchids at his Oakridge estate, mediates inter-family sit-downs and dotes on his nieces and nephews.

persons.name: Dante Lombardo
persons.current: A big earner with expensive tastes; ambitious for a crew of his own.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Danny Velvet. Smooth, silk-suited operator who runs Hunts Row Textile and Diamond Exchange and high-end commercial lending in the Racks.

persons.name: Darius Hollis
persons.current: Wants a title and a way out of the projects for his family.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Silk. Gifted young Black welterweight from the Eastside, managed by Louis Castelluccio.

persons.name: Declan Gallagher
persons.current: Wants steady port profits and a quiet Kerrytown; carries his brother's anger and does not trust Italian promises.
persons.public_identity_text: Manages the tugboat yards and South Pier skims with military discipline.

persons.name: Dennis McCaffrey
persons.current: Careful with his pension and his badge; keeps the precinct quiet.
persons.public_identity_text: Lieutenant who commands the station house at Mercer and 9th and knows every crap game and after-hours room in the precinct.

persons.name: Dominic Tarantino
persons.current: Cares about his crew's pay and the neighbourhood's feast days; dislikes change.
persons.role: Capo in the Castellano Family, South Hill crews
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Dom. Genial capo with a street-corner following on the South Hill.

persons.name: Edward Haggerty
persons.current: Wants a clean headline and to keep the union and the mayor happy.
persons.public_identity_text: Career cop, Kerrytown-born, who has run the department for six years.

persons.name: Enzo Moretti
persons.current: The family's cold strategic counsellor and quiet armorer.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as the Watchmaker. Don Sal's older brother; spends his days repairing antique clocks with a jeweler's loupe in a dusty Hunts Row storefront and takes the city bus home to his grandchildren.

persons.name: Eugene Cavallo
persons.current: A horse-player who likes his comforts and keeps a cash side practice.
persons.role: Attending trauma surgeon at Mercy General
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Stitch. Skilled surgeon who patches up the neighbourhood's wounded at 3:00 AM above a San Lorenzo pharmacy as a sideline.

persons.name: Francis Callahan
persons.current: Eyes the mayor's job and keeps his bargains on both sides of the aisle.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Frankie. Ward heeler who balances union backers and developers and wants the mayor's chair.

persons.name: Gennaro Moretti
persons.current: An aggressive expansionist who tests the other families' borders and thinks they have gone soft.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Gerry the Hook. Runs Eastside Auto Crush and the I-95 hijacking crews; spends Friday nights ringside at the Civic Arena or at after-hours smokers.

persons.name: Gerald Lockwood
persons.current: Cautious, social and fond of large, safe loans.
persons.role: President of First Harbor National Bank
persons.public_identity_text: Old-money banker who finances most of the city's construction.

persons.name: Gino Fabbri
persons.current: Keeps both places quiet and busy.
persons.role: Owner of Gino's Espresso Bar and Villa Roma
persons.public_identity_text: Old restaurateur who gives no sides his loyalty.

persons.name: Giuseppe Vannucci
persons.current: A patient old man who wants the family secure for his son and to be remembered as a man of respect.
persons.public_identity_text: Old Don Giuseppe, who led the Mercer Avenue and Ironworks crews out of the Castellano Family in 1967. Did hard time in Ironhaven; now keeps an unhurried routine with his barber, his wife and his son's business.

persons.name: Gordon Vance-Miller
persons.current: Methodical and stubborn; wants a case that survives appeal.
persons.role: Special Agent in Charge, organized crime
persons.public_identity_text: Patient federal agent who runs the Organized Crime Strike Force from the 12th floor.

persons.name: Harold Winslow
persons.current: Wants re-election and fewer headline failures.
persons.public_identity_text: Dignified old-money District Attorney with a cautious record on organised crime.

persons.name: Harrison Sterling III
persons.current: Wants to build something with his name on it and is leaning on borrowed money.
persons.public_identity_text: Old-money Oakridge developer assembling waterfront land for a future tower complex.

persons.name: Hector Rivera
persons.current: Pushes for wages and benefits for his members.
persons.role: President of Hotel and Restaurant Employees Local 211
persons.public_identity_text: Puerto Rican former waiter who leads the hotel and restaurant union.

persons.name: Ignazio Pellegrino
persons.current: Cautious; keeps his crews on a tight leash and dislikes unsanctioned skirmishes.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Iggy. Lean, pale veteran of the 1958 war who runs the family's day-to-day work from the Pompeii.

persons.name: Jackie Castellano
persons.current: Wants to modernize the port peacefully and keep his family out of trouble.
persons.public_identity_text: Matteo Castellano's nephew. Two years at the state university; calm, strategic young soldier who manages the North Pier checkers and keeps a working peace with Declan Gallagher.

persons.name: John Kavanagh
persons.current: Wants a title fight and loyalty from his neighbourhood.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as the Irish Hammer. Kerrytown heavyweight with a following in the Bricks, managed by Louis Castelluccio.

persons.name: Johnny Drago
persons.current: Reckless and eager; wants to be made quickly.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Handsome Johnny. Drives a flashy used Camaro, runs a Mercer Avenue sports book and volunteers for work to earn his button.

persons.name: Judith Katz
persons.current: Ambitious and underestimated by the men around her.
persons.public_identity_text: Quick, well-prepared prosecutor from a Jewish family in the Hill's edge neighbourhoods; handles felony cases and is trusted by the police.

persons.name: Leo Rosen
persons.current: Quiet, professional, careful with his time and references.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as the Torch. Independent technical specialist in the Racks, available to connected crews for hire.

persons.name: Liam Gallagher
persons.current: Angry over the 1973 dock strike killings and impatient with his brother's caution.
persons.public_identity_text: Declan's younger brother; drinks at the Harp and Crown and looks for excuses to ambush Castellano trucks.

persons.name: Lorenzo DeLuca
persons.current: Resents kicking up large envelopes to the elders while his men take the physical risks.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Larry Nails. Loud, barrel-chested owner of DeLuca Cadillac-Oldsmobile in Oakridge who runs the family's construction-site enforcement.

persons.name: Louis Castelluccio
persons.current: Loves fight night and the high life; always chasing the next big card.
persons.role: Boxing and music promoter, Tri-City Promotions
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Golden Boy. Runs Tri-City Promotions above the Civic Arena and manages young fighters.

persons.name: Lucia Vannucci
persons.current: Wants her family respected and her son safe; impatient with any slight to her husband.
persons.role: Wife of Giuseppe Vannucci; the family's matriarch
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Donna Lucia. Stern, devout matriarch who runs her husband's Oakridge home, feeds her son three nights a week and presses him on family honour.

persons.name: Marcus Vance
persons.current: Ambitious and modern-minded; wants clean, legitimate property so his people need no Italian laundering.
persons.role: Lieutenant in the Mercer Street Kings
persons.public_identity_text: Known as the Bishop. Runs the Kings' real estate office and wholesale supply like a business executive.

persons.name: Margaret Dunleavy
persons.current: Fiercely independent; takes no side.
persons.role: Owner of the Harp and Crown
persons.public_identity_text: Widow who owns the Harp and Crown and keeps order with a bat under the bar.

persons.name: Martin Keogh
persons.current: Likes a scoop; hungry for access.
persons.role: Crime columnist at the Daily Mirror
persons.public_identity_text: Known as the Nose. Star crime columnist whom rival crews use to leak tips.

persons.name: Marvin Kesselman
persons.current: Hungry for growth; careful about what he asks about the goods.
persons.role: Owner of Kesselman's Discount Electronics and Furs
persons.public_identity_text: Known as the Mink. Owner of a growing chain of discount electronics and fur showrooms.

persons.name: Matteo Castellano
persons.current: A hard working-class loyalist who trusts old friends, suspicious of anyone he does not know, and expects to run the family one day.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Matty the Bull. Hulking former longshoreman who holds court at the Pier 4 diner at 5:00 AM, drinking black coffee with union stewards and checking fish market prices.

persons.name: Matteo Russo
persons.current: A warm pastor who keeps what he hears.
persons.public_identity_text: Father Matteo, who hears the buttonmen's confessions, blesses Cadillacs and refuses to help the authorities.

persons.name: Maureen Tierney
persons.current: Wants a front-page story that matters.
persons.public_identity_text: Metro reporter at the Chronicle who covers City Hall and the courts.

persons.name: Michael Santoro
persons.current: A true believer in the family's code of honour, earned his button after three years in prison without talking; wants a crew of his own one day.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Mikey Saints. Sharp-dressed, disciplined young soldier who runs a small North Hill numbers route, pays imprisoned soldiers' wives down to the last dollar and coaches parish youth boxing.

persons.name: Nicolo Vannucci
persons.current: Dislikes the sleaze of Mercer Avenue but uses its cash flow to build the family's war chest; defers to his father.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Nicky. Impeccably tailored, somber son of the Boss who eats dinner with his mother three nights a week, oversees the sanitation carting and rarely smiles in public.

persons.name: Pasquale Ferrante
persons.current: Tired and thinking about Florida; wants a smooth handover and no wars before he steps down.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Patsy. Heavy, patient old-school underboss who runs the family's day-to-day business from the Vesuvio and the construction sites.

persons.name: Patrick Keane
persons.current: Wants the church's finances and reputation kept clean.
persons.public_identity_text: Archbishop with a Kerrytown childhood and a politician's patience.

persons.name: Paul Varga
persons.current: Personally loyal to Nicky Vannucci; looks after his mother and wants to be made.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Paulie the Hammer. Coaches suburban Little League on Saturdays and breaks legs at the Ironworks on Mondays.

persons.name: Pietro Castellano
persons.current: Wants the family to stay whole after him and is slowly handing more of the business to his nephew.
persons.public_identity_text: Old Don Pietro, a former longshoreman who built the family on the docks. Fading but still respected; receives visitors at a table in the back of a South Hill bakery.

persons.name: Raymond Doyle
persons.current: Wants to finish his term cleanly and hold the unions and developers happy.
persons.public_identity_text: Genial machine mayor, Irish-American, a Kerrytown man who rose through the ward clubs.

persons.name: Rico Basso
persons.current: Nicky's childhood blood-brother: fiercely loyal and hair-trigger violent.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as the Butcher. Former Golden Gloves heavyweight who runs San Lorenzo Provisions and the Starlight's bouncer crews.

persons.name: Rocco Lamberti
persons.current: Content to stay close to the boss; mildly resents the capos who treat him as furniture.
persons.role: Soldier in the Sabatini Family; Don Carmine's driver
persons.public_identity_text: Quiet, heavy driver and bodyguard who sits in the Don's kitchen and hears more than he says.

persons.name: Roland Whitcomb
persons.current: Values his reputation and his pension more than his dockets.
persons.public_identity_text: Superior Court judge of an old Protestant family; plays golf at the Oakridge club.

persons.name: Roy Pike
persons.current: Practical and blunt; wants the club to stay independent and profitable.
persons.role: President of the Iron Horsemen MC
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Diesel. Runs the machine shop on the Flats and the club's southern gun pipeline.

persons.name: Salvatore Conti
persons.current: Sees the old ceremonies as outdated superstition and cares about the numbers; a big earner who can quietly ignore small orders.
persons.role: Capo in the Sabatini Family, finance regime
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Sally Glasses. Bespectacled, mild-mannered elder who manages the Master Layoff Bank and reviews commercial loan portfolios at Villa Roma.

persons.name: Salvatore Marchetti
persons.current: Wants a winning team, a championship and an athletic director's chair.
persons.role: Head basketball coach, Saint Jude State
persons.public_identity_text: Known as the Deacon. Coach of the Friars, the state university's basketball team.

persons.name: Salvatore Moretti
persons.current: A veteran of the 1958 war who sees the city as a butcher's block where a man keeps only what he can defend.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Sal the Iron. Stoic, cigar-chomping patriarch who holds court in the basement of the Pompeii Social Club on Hunts Row, in work slacks and a cardigan, settling garment and trucking disputes.

persons.name: Sol Weiss
persons.current: Old, careful, meticulous; charges well and keeps his word.
persons.public_identity_text: Known as Inky. Independent forger in the Racks who can produce paper for those who need to leave town.

persons.name: Teresa Ianelli
persons.current: Fiercely protective of her father and of the company; ambitious but expects no one to hand her anything.
persons.role: Office manager of Saint Jude Ready-Mix; daughter of Carmine Sabatini

claims.text: In 1974 Carmine Sabatini quietly had his own brother-in-law and three rival contractors disappear into a deep bedrock pour so that the Concrete Club answered to him alone.

In 1973 Castellano crews used cargo hooks and shotguns to crush an independent longshoremen's strike on the South Piers. Among the dead was the older brother of Brendan O'Malley, which left a lasting blood grudge between the Castellanos and Kerrytown's Irish.

In 1946 a brutal three-month shooting war across Killbuck Point and the Hill (the Four-Corner Harbor War) ended in exhaustion and fixed the raw territorial divide between the families, the Iron Balance.
In 1958 Sal Moretti and his Eastside garment and trucking crews broke away from the Sabatini Family in a bloody six-month civil war and became the Moretti Family, the city's fourth sovereign family.
In 1967 Giuseppe Vannucci led the Mercer Avenue and Ironworks crews out of the Castellano Family and took independent control of the Strip and the steel foundries.
